text: The Fed just hiked rates to 3.75%-4% with another increase signaled — this is a meaningful shift back to tightening that raises borrowing costs and puts pressure on high-valuation and unprofitable growth stocks in your portfolio, so tighten risk across the board.

IONQ is 46% off its high with no profits, negative free cash flow, 10% short interest, and bearish technicals — reduce your exposure in a rising-rate environment that punishes unprofitable companies hardest.
MSTR acts as a leveraged Bitcoin bet with negative 36% free cash flow and 8% short interest — in a rate-hiking cycle, trim this speculative position to a size you can stomach losing.
UNH at a PE of 16.7 with nearly 12% revenue growth and a 4.7% free cash flow yield is exactly the kind of profitable, defensive name that holds up well when rates are rising — add on this weakness.
GOOGL trading at a PE of 23 with 15% revenue growth and insider buying offers solid value below its moving averages — a reasonable spot to add to a fundamentally strong position.
